title: Jarl: new records kind and priority without saying they were defaulted
claim: A task filed without --kind is recorded as kind bug with no note, while the tier default gets one; the report filed a film as a bug and saw it days later in models.
evidence: new "Film of the whole epic for the tester and the PO" on a copy of the 6.2.0 loop printed 'parsed: priority 2 · tier standard · kind bug' and a note for tier only. Map row fr-01.
where: JarlSkill/skills/jarl/scripts/lib/commands.mjs (cmdNew), at release/6.2.1 71ebc5b after the split; jarl-lib.mjs:1548 at a1132a8
proposal: Print one defaulted note per value not given (kind, priority), as for tier.
verifier: fresh Opus sceptic, 2026-11-03, at JarlSkill a1132a8: stands. True: kind falls to the profile default and is printed in the parsed line, but only tier gets a 'defaulted' note; and at a1132a8 Kind has no command to correct it afterwards, so a wrong default sticks. Covered by: 6.3.0 (was 6.2.1) #029 partly (makes Kind editable).

surfaces: docs:the-lock + prime (rules.ts Log management) + knowledge:log-management vs code/live CLI
claim: The log gate is all-or-nothing: if ANY log_required node is missing its entry, --approve fills nothing at all, no pair on any node.
evidence:
docs/the-lock.md:135: "at `--approve`, if *any* `log_required` node is missing its entry, the run fills **nothing at all** — no pair on any node, related or not."
Prime (templates/rules.ts:282-285): "if ANY `log_required` node's source drifted with no fresh entry, `--approve` fills NOTHING that run (no pair on any node is verified)".
knowledge log-management.ts:108-112: same wording.
Code core/fill-classify.ts:232-236: "The log gate's set: every component owning an unverified pair … for (const p of unverifiedPairs) nodeSet.add(p.nodePath)"; core/fill.ts:411-427 gates only nodeSet.
Live: type `lib` (log_required, no rules), source changed, no entry; svc2 pair unverified with entry. `yg check --approve --only-deterministic` printed "fill  1 pair · 1 script (free) … fill  done in 0s — 1 passed" then "yg check: FAIL  1 error … error[log-entry-missing] 1 node changed with no log entry  at: lib". The run was not ABORTED.
truth: The gate only stops the fill when a component that owns an unverified pair (a pair this run would fill) lacks its entry. A drifted log_required component with no pairs to fill (a rule-less node, all rules draft) does not stop the fill. It only shows as a read-only log-entry-missing error in the post-fill report.
fix: Either gate on every drifted log_required node, as documented, or reword the-lock, prime and log-management: the fill stops when any component it would fill owes an entry; other unlogged components block the report, not the fill.

v.reason: Reproduced live. With lib (log_required, no rules) left without an entry, `yg check --approve --only-deterministic` still filled 2 script pairs and then reported error[log-entry-missing] at lib, with no ABORTED. fill-classify.ts:232-236 builds the gate set only from nodes that own unverified pairs. So the-lock.md:135 ('fills nothing at all — no pair on any node, related or not'), prime rules.ts:282-285 and the knowledge topic are all wrong for a drifted node that has no pairs. The practical impact is small because the report still goes red, so severity is lowered to minor.

title: Kotlin 2.2+ syntax swallows the rest of the file into one ERROR node, so later declarations vanish. Imports of them get no edge, and an ambiguous silence can turn into one arbitrary edge
evidence: Parse of `package com.acme.payments / import ... / val tpl = $$"price: $$amount" / class PaymentService / class Other` gives `ERROR "val tpl = $$...\nclass PaymentService" [2:0-5:0]`, so every declaration from that line to EOF sits inside the ERROR node. When guards (`is String if x.isEmpty() ->`) and `context(log: Logger)` do the same. Probe cases through runCase on 0.27.0: zz-kt-guard-in-target-decl, zz-kt-multidollar-in-target-decl and zz-kt-context-in-target-decl all fail with `expected edge src/c/Use.kt:2->pay not emitted (got none)`. The importing file's own import survives (zz-kt-*-user-import pass). The declaring file's classes do not. False-positive check: zz-kt-guard-flips-ambiguity (the kotlin-same-fqn-two-files-ambiguous-silence layout, plus a when-guard above `class Thing` in src/x) fails with `unexpected cross-node edge src/z/Use.kt:2->y`. That breaks the matrix header's 'ZERO false positives' invariant. The realistic trigger is KMP expect/actual, where the same FQN lives in 2 files. No stable Kotlin grammar fixes this (see GF-9).
impact: Kotlin 2.2 features (guards, multi-dollar strings) and 2.4 context parameters are stable and common. One such line anywhere above a class removes that class from the SymbolTable. Every import of it from other nodes then silently yields no dependency, and the relation check passes code it never saw. Deterministic rules that walk class_declaration also miss those classes. The palette documents only the local 'type ref invisible' effect, not the loss of declarations for the whole file.
suggested_fix: In kotlin.ts, add an ERROR-tolerant declaration fallback. When a top-level ERROR node exists, re-scan its token children for `class|object|interface|typealias|fun` + identifier at depth 0, or re-parse the ERROR's byte range after the offending statement. Alternatively, mark the file 'declarations incomplete' and silence every resolution that would bind into, or disambiguate through, that file (fail-closed rather than flipping an ambiguity to an edge). Add the three zz-kt cases and the ambiguity-flip case to the palette as traps.
verifier: I reproduced this on the shipped kotlin wasm with web-tree-sitter 0.27.0 ($TMPDIR/verify-grammars-wts/probe2.mjs). The line `val tpl = $$"price: $$amount"` produces `ERROR [2:0-5:0]`, and that node contains both following classes. A when-guard and `context(log: Logger)` each produce one ERROR that runs to EOF. The control file with a plain `"a${s}"` string parses cleanly. Live CLI, pay/Pay.kt declaring PaymentService and c/Use.kt importing it: with no relation declared, the control fails with `relation-undeclared-dependency c/Use.kt:2 → pay`. The $$, guard and context variants each report `yg check: PASS` ($TMPDIR/verify-grammars-k0..k3), so a real dependency goes undetected. Ambiguity flip: the kotlin-same-fqn-two-files-ambiguous-silence layout passes, but after a when-guard is added above `class Thing` in src/x the check fails with `src/z/Use.kt:2 → y` ($TMPDIR/verify-grammars-kamb-guard). That is a false edge, against the matrix's 'ZERO false positives' invariant (kotlin-name-resolution-matrix.test.ts:24). The palette case kotlin-context-parameter-type-silent.md documents only the local type-ref gap, not the loss of every declaration to the end of the file. kotlin.ts declarations() walks only DECLARATION_TYPES nodes, so nothing inside an ERROR is keyed. Both a missed dependency and a wrong edge are reproducible.
